newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 7.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Most prices finished flat to lower on Thursday in quiet trading, Random Lengths said in its weekly cash market review. Dealers bided their time, waiting for job sites to dry out or thaw out so they could move already-sold wood from their yards. Treaters put off building inventories, the agency said.

The tendency to wait on purchases was reinforced by the hefty premium of prices to year-ago levels. Encouraged by feedback about low inventories in the pipeline, mills were inclined to let order files dwindle and delay cutting prices until the last minute, Random Lengths said.

Some producers said they were not getting enough empty rail cars and figured there was no reason to open counters if they couldn't load the wood anyway. Delays in rail shipments caused by the slow return of empties pushed some dealers to buy more truckloads from distribution yards and reloads to tide them over until carloads arrived, the reporting agency said.
Rumors that some Canadian producers who had run out of fee-free and $50 wood were refusing to ship to the U.S. rather than pay fees of $100 per thousand failed to move buyers.

Office wholesalers took advantage of deals on quick wood to put together a steady volume of back-to-back business. However, other secondaries had to discount stock bought earlier to keep it moving. The Federal Reserve's decision not to raise interest rates had been expected and scarcely caused a ripple.
A few hot spots in the market remained. Southern Pine radius edge decking continued higher, and timbers also registered solid gains in the South.
Last week's fire at a large mill in British Columbia contributed to tight supplies of 22- and 24-foot and pushed more demand to other species, Random Lengths said.
